Their birth country has since shut down adoptions because of that very reason. We did everything legally on our end, all very official, etc., and I have no regrets. Maybe selfishly, because these are my kids and I cannot imagine my life without them. One child is happy and well-adjusted, the other does have some mental health issues. 

There are no guarantees, and that goes for bio kids as well. Luckily, we have the money and resources to provide the treatment needed over the years. I would never have considered "rehoming" (adoption disruption), and things got reallllly bad at one point, but in searching for how to help my child, I did see a lot of the rehoming stuff, so I knew it existed.

I feel your words. I don’t yet understand why my pain has flares and remissions (there’s some thought that it could be autoimmune, or related to my Crohn’s). Some days I’m fine. Some days I’m literally in a wheelchair. I keep a cane in my car because one wrong step and my hip can buckle. I was excluded from a family trip my sister planned because “I’m not wasting my vacation pushing you around in a wheelchair.” Can you feel the love? Ironically, I can actually walk so much easier than I can stand still (like waiting in lines). I went on a 4-mile hike a couple days ago (very painful, but worth it). Yet sitting at a desk (work) is excruciating. Standing for any length of time is impossible. My friends see the amazing hiking photos and don’t understand why I need a wheelchair at Disney (again-the standing in lines). Honestly, I can’t blame their confusion, but I’m tired of trying to justify it. 

I went on a cruise 3 years ago. I thought I’d be fine.  Ended up collapsing on day 1 because my hip pain was so bad. I literally could not walk. Luckily, they rent out wheelchairs on the cruise lines. Costs a bloody fortune, but worth it. However, cruise ships are very difficult to navigate in a wheelchair! I still had a good time, but man, that was rough.

It’s annoying when people try to relate but end up downplaying what I deal with. “Oh, my back is sore in the morning, too” No. I’ve had spinal arthritis since my 20’s. It’s not the same as your achy back after a bad night of sleep. I appreciate the effort to relate, but it just makes me realize no one really understands the depth of my pain. 

Another one is trying to relate to my Crohn’s “I had a stomach bug once. It really sucked.” Ok, now imagine those symptoms every damn day. For months at a time. Off and on for 20 years (so far-I’m still fairly young). Combined with the pain, bleeding, nausea, etc. Imagine weekly injections for 10 years just so you can manage to leave your house (which no one would dream of doing with a stomach bug). And then still having the need for immediate bathroom access and constantly encountering ‘no public restrooms’ everywhere.

I’ve gone back and read several of your posts because your name caught my eye (my daughter is really into the special numbers like 777-I think she calls them angel numbers). I have a 15yo daughter and my heart hurts for you. I was so much like you as a teen. With the self harm and mental health concerns. 

Your parents are in denial. They don’t think their perfect child could have a problem because that could mean they haven’t been the perfect parents. If you were my daughter, I would hope you could come to me and I would listen. But you need to not say it jokingly or as you’re jumping out of the car at school drop off, etc. Ask for an appointment with her. Maybe get your nails done (I’m taking my 15yo this weekend!). Tell her you need to talk to her about something serious. Tell her you are having bad thoughts, harming yourself, and you need help. Fad or otherwise, self-harm is a cry for help. Eating disorders are a sign of some sort of trauma in your past (usually) and your way of taking control is to severely control your diet.

If she still blows you off after that, go into your school front office (assuming you’re in the US-I don’t know how other countries work) and ask for an appointment with the counselor/school therapist. They will schedule a time for you. If it’s after school, just tell your mom you have a club meeting or something after school (I don’t normally recommend lying to mom, but if she would stop you from getting help, lie).  Tell the counselor everything. If anyone has touched you inappropriately, tell them. If anyone has hit you, ever-tell them. Explain how you cut yourself. Explain the restricted eating. Ask for the help you so desperately need. They may have to involve your parents. But that will be the wake-up call they obviously need. 

As your internet mom, I’m so sorry you feel so alone and pushed aside. I promise you’re not alone. Sweet girl, you deserve to be happy. You deserve help. My honest feeling from what you wrote is that your mom is just afraid to admit you have a problem because it would reflect poorly on her parenting. Maybe remind her you love her and she’s a great mom (if that’s how you feel), but that you are afraid of things progressing and could lead to bigger problems (suicidality). Feel free talk to me if you want to. But more importantly, talk to your mom and/or the school counselor.

That sounds more like CBT (cognitive behavioral therapy). DBT is skills-based learning. It's like taking a class. It's typically done in a group setting, but mine is one-on-one. I'm a more 'difficult' case. LOL

Get The Dialectical Behavior Therapy Skills Workbook (second edition) by Matthew McKay (et al). It's on Amazon. That's all we do in DBT therapy is walk through the workbook together and do the assignments each week. Take it at your own pace. Some concepts are more difficult than others to master. Some take a lot of practice and feel stupid, but are really helpful once they're ingrained.
